Oat and vegetable patties: 2 tablespoons mashed boiled chickpeas
1 tablespoon finely chopped parsley
Squeeze the vegetables, mix with all the ingredients and leave for 10 minutes.
Shape flat walnut-sized patties.
Bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes until lightly golden on both sides (turn at 10 minutes).
Let cool and serve.
A good source of protein and fibre for meat-free days.
Avocado and banana mash
2 tablespoons ripe avocado
2 tablespoons ripe banana
Wash and peel the fruit.
Mash completely with a fork.
Serve straight after making, at an age-appropriate texture.
1 small ripe pear
A little drinking water if needed
Wash and peel the pear and remove the core.
If it’s firm, cook with a little water until soft.
Mash and serve lukewarm.
2 tablespoons fine oats
Half an apple
Peel and core the apple and grate it.
Cook with the oats and water until very soft.
Let cool and serve at a suitable texture.
Avocado mash with well-cooked egg
1 fully cooked egg
Cook the egg until both the yolk and white are completely set.
Mash well together with the avocado.
Serve at a suitable texture; keep the egg allergen in mind.
Lentil and vegetable patties
3 tablespoons well-cooked red lentils
2 tablespoons cooked carrot
1 tablespoon fine oats
Mash all the ingredients well.
Form soft small patties.
Bake until completely cooked inside and break up appropriately.
Yogurt with oats and peach
2 tablespoons plain pasteurised yogurt
2 tablespoons cooked oats
Half a ripe peach
Cook the oats completely with water and let them cool.
Peel the peach and mash very well.
Mix with the yogurt and serve straight away.
Soft apple-cinnamon pancakes
3 tablespoons fine oats
Half a grated apple
A very little cinnamon, optional
Mix the ingredients until smooth.
In a non-stick pan, cook small pancakes completely on both sides.
Serve soft, broken into age-appropriate pieces.
Mini vegetable pizzas
1 small wholemeal lavash
2 tablespoons grated tomato
2 tablespoons grated low-salt kashar
2 tablespoons finely chopped red pepper and mushrooms
A pinch of thyme
Cut 4–5 rounds out of the lavash with the rim of a glass.
Spread with tomato, divide the vegetables and kashar on top and sprinkle with thyme.
Bake for 8–10 minutes until the cheese melts and the edges are golden.
Let cool, slice and serve.
Using fresh tomato instead of ready-made pizza sauce reduces salt and sugar.
Green beans with meat
60 g finely diced beef
1 cup chopped green beans
1 small tomato, grated
1 tablespoon finely chopped onion
Cook the meat in olive oil, covered, for 10 minutes until it reabsorbs its own juices.
Add the onion and toss for 2 minutes, then add the tomato and toss for 2 minutes.
Add the beans and hot water; cook over a low heat for 35–40 minutes until the meat and beans are tender.
Pull the meat into small shreds and cut the beans into 1 cm lengths.
Cooking the meat in a pressure cooker shortens the time and makes it more tender.
Baked salmon and potatoes
70 g boneless salmon fillet
1 small potato, thinly sliced
A few sprigs of dill
A few drops of lemon juice
Toss the potato slices with olive oil, arrange on a tray and bake for 15 minutes.
Place the salmon next to the potatoes and add dill and lemon.
Bake 12–15 more minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Check for bones and break into small pieces.
Fish is recommended 1–2 times a week.
Spinach and lor cheese börek fingers
1 sheet yufka
1 cup finely chopped spinach
Wilt the spinach in olive oil for 3 minutes, cool and mix with the lor cheese.
Whisk the egg and milk; cut the yufka into 4 triangles and brush each with this mixture.
Put the filling on the wide edge, roll into fingers and brush the tops with the remaining mixture.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until golden on top; let cool and serve.
Lor cheese is a low-salt option.
Lentil and bulgur patties (soft)
1 dessert spoon tomato paste (low salt)
1 tablespoon finely chopped spring onion
A few sprigs of parsley
Cook the lentils in the water for 15 minutes until they break down.
Remove from the heat, add the bulgur and leave covered for 20 minutes to swell.
Toss the spring onion and tomato paste in olive oil for 2 minutes and add to the mixture.
Add the parsley, knead and shape small, soft patties.
Serve on a lettuce leaf or a plate.
Don’t use hot pepper or isot.
Chicken and vegetable sauté with yogurt
80 g chicken breast, small cubes
Half a zucchini and half a carrot, finely chopped
Cook the chicken in olive oil for 6–7 minutes until white on every side.
Add the vegetables and soften, covered, for 10 minutes; add 2 spoonfuls of water if needed.
Remove from the heat when the chicken is completely cooked inside.
Once lukewarm, serve with yogurt and thyme.
Don’t add yogurt to hot food; it curdles.
Without the yogurt, 24 hours in the fridge.
Banana oat pancakes
4 tablespoons fine rolled oats
Mash the banana well with a fork; mix with the egg, oats and cinnamon.
Rest the mixture for 5 minutes.
Lightly grease a non-stick pan with butter and spoon in small rounds.
Cook each side over a low heat for 2 minutes until the centre is cooked.
The banana’s sweetness is enough; don’t add sugar or honey.
24 hours in the fridge; can be frozen.

50 g boiled, shredded chicken
2 tablespoons peas
2 tablespoons finely diced carrot
